description: Worker probe:smoke fails with 'auth bootstrap failed — Keycloak unreachable' even though the Keycloak container is healthy. Root cause: stack-up-docker.sh allocates dynamic ports per worker (KEYCLOAK_PORT=37xxx, APP_PROXY_PORT=36xxx) and exports them into docker compose, but the worker's root .env keeps the static boilerplate defaults (9080, 4181) inherited from stack-env-hydrate.sh's copy-from-canonical step. Anything that reads .env via dotenv (pnpm probe:smoke, db:migrate:deploy, integration tests, the API at boot) sees the stale port and tries to talk to 127.0.0.1:9080 which is never published. Builders historically lose entire iterations chasing this as if it were a Keycloak realm/seed bug.
resolution: Two complementary fixes (commit pending in scripts/stack-up-docker.sh + scripts/probe-bootstrap.sh): (1) stack-up-docker.sh upserts KEYCLOAK_PORT, APP_PROXY_PORT, PG_PORT, API_PORT, NEXT_PORT, OAUTH_ISSUER_URL, OAUTH_JWKS_URL, OAUTH2_PROXY_REDIRECT_URL, OAUTH2_PROXY_WHITELIST_DOMAIN, NEXT_PUBLIC_POST_LOGOUT_REDIRECT_URI, NEXT_PUBLIC_OIDC_LOGOUT_ENDPOINT, NEXT_PUBLIC_OAUTH2_PROXY_CLIENT_ID into the worker's .env right after port allocation. Worker-only — canonical app-dev-host .env stays static. (2) probe-bootstrap.sh's hydrate_stack_runtime_env now writes the same values into .env as a safety net so probe:smoke survives even if stack:up was skipped or the .env drifted. Also persists exports to .env.runtime (gitignored) so the next bash subshell in the && pipeline can source them. Both are idempotent and have regression tests in scripts/__tests__/.

description: pnpm probe:smoke is three commands chained with &&: 'bash scripts/probe-bootstrap.sh && pnpm openapi:check && bash scripts/probe-run-with-ownership-check.sh'. Each segment runs in its own bash subshell, so anything probe-bootstrap.sh exports via 'export VAR=...' or 'eval source-runtime-env-file' dies at the first &&. Subsequent segments only see env they read from the OS process env at their own start (pnpm/dotenv-loaded .env, etc.).
resolution: Don't rely on in-process exports across the && chain. Either persist into .env (dotenv picks it up at next pnpm boot) or write to .env.runtime that downstream callers source explicitly. probe-bootstrap.sh now does both.

description: OAuth/Keycloak hostname strategy: SINGLE hostname (keycloak.localtest.me) used by every consumer. The original failure was a builder probe getting tokens with iss=A while the api validated against iss=B; the obvious fix is 'pick whichever hostname both share' but that breaks one of the two consumer classes (browsers OR panel-container probes). Two consumer classes need to reach Keycloak: (a) real browsers from the primary `app-dev-host` stack (humans logging in) — can resolve *.localtest.me via public wildcard DNS to 127.0.0.1, CANNOT resolve Docker-only hostnames like host.docker.internal. (b) server-side processes in containers (api, oauth2-proxy, the SFX panel running probe:smoke against worker stacks) — can resolve hostnames declared in extra_hosts. keycloak.localtest.me is the only hostname that satisfies both classes, so it is the canonical choice.
resolution: Pin OAUTH_ISSUER_URL/JWKS_URL/whitelist on keycloak.localtest.me everywhere. Make every container that needs server-side Keycloak access declare 'keycloak.localtest.me:host-gateway' in extra_hosts: (1) sfx-apps-boilerplate/docker-compose.yml api + app-oauth2-proxy services (regression test in scripts/__tests__/oauth2-proxy-compose.test.mjs). (2) sfx-team-panel/docker-compose.yml panel service (this was the missing piece — panel only had host.docker.internal mapped, so probe:smoke from inside it failed). For an already-running panel without a restart, hot-patch /etc/hosts: docker exec --user root sfx-team-panel-panel-1 sh -c 'echo "$(getent hosts host.docker.internal | awk "{print \$1}") keycloak.localtest.me app.localtest.me" >> /etc/hosts'. Browser-facing redirect URIs use app.localtest.me (also wildcard). Keep host.docker.internal:host-gateway in extra_hosts for Linux portability of non-OAuth tooling (db tunnels, port forwarders).

description: Original probe failure that led to the single-hostname decision (mx-c1a32f). Symptom: probe:smoke gets a valid token from Keycloak but every authenticated request returns 401 'Invalid token issuer'. Root cause was that the panel container had only host.docker.internal in extra_hosts — no keycloak.localtest.me — so probe-bootstrap fell back to host.docker.internal when fetching tokens. Keycloak start-dev mints iss=<request-host>, so tokens carried iss=host.docker.internal:<port> while the api validated against OAUTH_ISSUER_URL=keycloak.localtest.me:<port>. Initial wrong fix was to swap everything to host.docker.internal — worked for probes but broke real-browser logins on the primary stack (Chrome can't resolve Docker-only hostnames). Cost a builder ~70 minutes of looping diagnostics.
resolution: See mx-c1a32f for the right architectural answer. Lesson: when picking a hostname for a service consumed by both real browsers and server-side containers, the candidate hostname must be resolvable from BOTH — wildcard DNS entries (*.localtest.me) plus extra_hosts on every container that needs server-side access. Never use Docker-only hostnames (host.docker.internal) for any URL that ends up in a redirect_uri or token iss claim that a browser will eventually see.

description: @anatine/zod-openapi 2.2.6 cannot extract metadata from .openapi() if it is chained AFTER .optional() or .nullable(). Wrong order compiles cleanly and unit tests on the schema itself pass, but generateSchema(schema) throws TypeError 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading metaOpenApi)' at NestJS module load when @ApiBody/@ApiResponse decorators evaluate, killing the api before it can serve a single request. Symptom in the logs is a stack ending at packages/validation/src/openapi.ts -> generateSchema -> @anatine/zod-openapi/src/lib/zod-openapi.ts:316.
resolution: .openapi() MUST come BEFORE .optional() and .nullable() on every Zod field. Canonical pattern: z.string().openapi({description:'x'}).optional() and z.string().openapi({description:'x'}).nullable().optional(). See packages/validation/src/schemas/common.schema.ts for the reference shape — every existing schema follows this order. If you upgrade @anatine/zod-openapi past 2.2.6, retest both orderings before relaxing this rule.

description: apps/api Dockerfile builds @sfx/domain, @sfx/shared, @sfx/validation, @sfx/database to dist at IMAGE BUILD TIME (development stage). docker-compose.yml bind-mounts only packages/<x>/src into the running container, NOT packages/<x>/dist. Result: when a worker (or any branch) adds a new schema/entity to packages/*/src after the image was built, the running container has src visible but dist still reflects the canonical boilerplate's version — the new export resolves to undefined at @sfx/api boot, surfacing as 'Cannot read properties of undefined' inside whatever decorator first uses the missing export.
resolution: apps/api/package.json dev script now runs `pnpm -r --filter @sfx/domain --filter @sfx/shared --filter @sfx/validation --filter @sfx/database run build` before `nest start -b swc --watch`. Adds ~3-4s to api container boot but guarantees dist matches src on every container start, including after stack:reset/stack:up cycles in worker stacks. The Dockerfile still builds packages at image build time — the dev script is a safety net, not a replacement.

description: stack-up-docker.sh emits '[stack-up] WARN: /etc/hosts is missing host.docker.internal entry' every time pnpm stack:up runs inside the SFX panel container. The warning is a false positive in container context: Docker Desktop and Linux Docker provide host.docker.internal via the container's DNS resolver / extra_hosts mapping, NOT via /etc/hosts. The grep for `^127.0.0.1[[:space:]]+host.docker.internal` in /etc/hosts always fails inside containers, regardless of whether host.docker.internal actually resolves (which it does, via DNS). Probe agents see this warning on every iteration and chase it as if it were a real config gap.
resolution: Gate the /etc/hosts check on `[ ! -f /.dockerenv ]`. The /.dockerenv marker file is created by every official Docker image at build time, so its absence means we're on a real host — exactly the case where the warning IS valid (host browser hitting host.docker.internal:<port> DOES need the /etc/hosts entry, since Docker Desktop only adds host.docker.internal to container DNS, not to the host /etc/hosts). Inside any container the marker is present and the warning is suppressed. Regression test in scripts/__tests__/stack-up-docker.test.mjs asserts the gating expression is in place.
